Treatment summary
Patient presented flolowing a side-impact collision at an intersection with acute pain and swelling of the right knee. Over nine
visits, care consisted of clinical examination, range-of-motion assessment, activity modification, and a structured home exercise
program. Some examination findings, including localized tenderness and mild effusion, are consistent with a soft-tissue injury to
the knee, while other orthopedic tests, including ligamentous stability assessment, returned normal results. At this stage it
remains unclaer whether the presenting symptoms originate entirely from this incident, and further evaluation may help clarify
the contribution. No prior injury to the same body region is documented in available records. Treatment followed a typical
clinical course, with visit frequency decreasing as symptoms improved and function returned. Billed services reflect the care

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page

- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
